correctness.rationale: The parity step is exact: an even common value would force two odd terms two apart to be squares; an odd common value forces every even term to be a square or twice a square. A five-term block beginning at an even integer would then contain three even terms, two of the same type, which is impossible at gaps \(2\) or \(4\). For an odd start, the two even terms must have opposite types, yielding the two Pell equations and the displayed divisor-sum identities by multiplicativity of \(\sigma\). Standard descent by the unit \(3-2\sqrt2\) proves the two Pell parametrizations. The finite \(10^{38}\) cutoff is replayed from the packaged paths with deterministic factorization; all \(50\) residuals are nonzero.

originality.rationale: The focal paper proves only that a six-term constant run is impossible; its parity argument leaves the five-term boundary open when the block starts odd. The present result identifies the exact two Pell families for that boundary, derives additional divisor-sum identities, proves logarithmic sparsity of candidate starts, and eliminates every candidate below \(10^{38}\). The adjacent-pair discussion on MathOverflow contains the basic square-or-twice-square parity observation but not the five-term Pell reduction. Targeted semantic, exact-phrase, and database searches did not locate the theorem or an implication covering it.
residual_risks: An equivalent elementary five-term reduction may exist in an unindexed note or unpublished computation.
The theorem does not establish global nonexistence beyond the exact \(10^{38}\) cutoff.

value.rationale: The focal paper leaves five as the only possible extremal run length for the proper-divisor-sum function. The present theorem attacks exactly that natural boundary rather than an arbitrary slice: it converts a putative maximal run into two explicit Pell-divisor equations, reducing \(X\) possible starts to only \(O(\log X)\) candidates. The exact \(10^{38}\) exclusion then gives a very large, reproducible finite cutoff obtained from the structural reduction rather than a raw integer scan. This supplies both a reusable route for further global work and a concrete strengthening of the published extremal result.
